ANSWER: In the logistic regression remission(PR=1, PD/SD=0) ~ Age + BMI + Gender (Female=0/Male=1), the Age coefficient is -0.0795 (SE 0.0263, 95% CI [-0.131, -0.028], p=0.0025). This is the change in log-odds of remission per one-year increase in patient age: each additional year of age reduces the log-odds of remission by ~0.08 (odds ratio ≈ 0.924/year), holding BMI and gender constant.

DETAILED RESULTS
- n = 80 complete cases (41 empty trailing rows dropped; no imputation; 0 missing in Age/BMI/Gender/Efficacy among the 80).
- Outcome split: remission = 41 (all PR), non-remission = 39 (22 PD + 17 SD).
- Model: statsmodels Logit, MLE, main effects + intercept, Age continuous (not centered/rescaled).
- Convergence: converged=True, 5 iterations, 0 warnings. Pseudo R-squared = 0.124; LLR p=0.0033.

Full coefficient table:
  Intercept   1.5313  (SE 2.7755, p=0.581)
  Age        -0.0795  (SE 0.0263, 95% CI [-0.1311, -0.0280], p=0.0025)  <-- the answer
  BMI         0.1621  (SE 0.1088, p=0.136)
  Gender_male -0.6132 (SE 0.5471, p=0.262)  [Male vs Female ref]

The Age coefficient (-0.0795) is exactly the quantity asked: the change in log-odds of remission per one-year increase in age. Cross-checked with an independent explicit-design-matrix fit (statsmodels.api + add_constant) -> identical coefficients.
